sn1.60:1.1: This short discourse serves for the Buddha to articulate a naturalistic theory of poetry.
sn1.60:2.1: Rig Veda 10.90.9 says that verses, chants, and metres were born from the sacrifice.
sn1.60:2.2: The _akkhara_ (“syllable”) is the smallest indivisible morpheme, typically consisting of a consonant bound with a vowel. But it also has a mystical significance, the “imperishable” Divinity within all things.
